title: CDL Hazmat driving, parking and training study guide
description: CDL Hazmat study guide: attending, parking, smoking, fueling, tires, explosives documents, routing and hazmat training under 49 CFR 397 and 172.
intro: The driving and parking rules in 49 CFR Part 397 apply to motor carriers, their supervisors and the people who operate or are in charge of a vehicle carrying hazardous materials that must be marked or placarded, and 49 CFR Part 172 Subpart H sets the training requirements for hazmat employees. This guide sets out what the rule text states on who Part 397 covers, attending and parking vehicles, fires, smoking, fueling, tires, the documents carried with Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 (explosive) materials, the routing rules as they affect drivers, and hazmat training: who must be trained, what it covers, when it is due and what records are kept. Many rules apply only to explosives or only to Class 7 (radioactive) materials, so the exact words matter. The hazardous materials endorsement also needs a TSA security threat assessment and a State knowledge test; this guide covers neither, and goraedu does not issue endorsements. Your State may have its own requirements, so check them too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

points.text: Part 397 applies to each motor carrier transporting hazardous materials by a motor vehicle that must be marked or placarded in accordance with 177.823.
points.quote: The rules in this part apply to each motor carrier engaged in the transportation of hazardous materials by a motor vehicle which must be marked or placarded in accordance with § 177.823 of this title

points.text: It also applies to each officer or employee of the motor carrier who performs supervisory duties related to the transportation of hazardous materials, and to each person who operates or is in charge of a motor vehicle containing hazardous materials.
points.quote: (1) Each officer or employee of the motor carrier who performs supervisory duties related to the transportation of hazardous materials; and (2) Each person who operates or who is in charge of a motor vehicle containing hazardous materials.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.1, Application of the rules in this part (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A motor carrier or other person covered by Part 397 must comply with the rules in Parts 390 through 397 when transporting hazardous materials by a motor vehicle that must be marked or placarded in accordance with 177.823.
points.quote: A motor carrier or other person to whom this part is applicable must comply with the rules in parts 390 through 397, inclusive, of this subchapter when he/she is transporting hazardous materials by a motor vehicle which must be marked or placarded in accordance with § 177.823 of this title.

points.text: A motor vehicle containing hazardous materials must be driven and parked in compliance with the laws, ordinances and regulations of the jurisdiction where it is operated, unless they are at variance with specific DOT regulations that apply to that vehicle's operation and impose a more stringent obligation or restraint.

points.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, a motor vehicle which contains a Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 (explosive) material must be attended at all times by its driver or a qualified representative of the motor carrier that operates it.

points.quote: The vehicle is located on the property of a motor carrier, on the property of a shipper or consignee of the explosives, in a safe haven, or, in the case of a vehicle containing 50 pounds or less of a Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 material, on a construction or survey site

points.text: The lawful bailee of the explosives must also be aware of the nature of the explosives and have been instructed in the emergency procedures, and the vehicle must be within the bailee's unobstructed field of view or located in a safe haven.
points.quote: (2) The lawful bailee of the explosives is aware of the nature of the explosives the vehicle contains and has been instructed in the procedures which must be followed in emergencies; and (3) The vehicle is within the bailee's unobstructed field of view or is located in a safe haven.

points.text: A vehicle containing hazardous materials other than Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 materials that is on a public street or highway, or the shoulder of a public highway, must be attended by its driver.
points.quote: A motor vehicle which contains hazardous materials other than Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3, materials, and which is located on a public street or highway, or the shoulder of a public highway, must be attended by its driver.

points.text: That vehicle need not be attended while its driver is performing duties which are incident and necessary to the driver's duties as the operator of the vehicle.
points.quote: However, the vehicle need not be attended while its driver is performing duties which are incident and necessary to the driver's duties as the operator of the vehicle.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.5, Attendance and surveillance of motor vehicles (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A vehicle is attended when the person in charge is on the vehicle, awake and not in a sleeper berth, or is within 100 feet of the vehicle and has it within an unobstructed field of view.
points.quote: A motor vehicle is attended when the person in charge of the vehicle is on the vehicle, awake, and not in a sleeper berth, or is within 100 feet of the vehicle and has it within his/her unobstructed field of view.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.5, Attendance and surveillance of motor vehicles (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A qualified representative of a motor carrier has been designated by the carrier to attend the vehicle, is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials in it, has been instructed in the emergency procedures, and is authorized to move the vehicle and has the means and ability to do so.
points.quote: A qualified representative of a motor carrier is a person who— (i) Has been designated by the carrier to attend the vehicle; (ii) Is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials contained in the vehicle he/she attends; (iii) Has been instructed in the procedures he/she must follow in emergencies; and (iv) Is authorized to move the vehicle and has the means and ability to do so.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.5, Attendance and surveillance of motor vehicles (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A safe haven is an area specifically approved in writing by local, State or Federal governmental authorities for the parking of unattended vehicles containing Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 materials.
points.quote: A safe haven is an area specifically approved in writing by local, State, or Federal governmental authorities for the parking of unattended vehicles containing Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials.

points.text: A vehicle containing Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 materials must not be parked on or within 5 feet of the traveled portion of a public street or highway.
points.quote: A motor vehicle which contains Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials must not be parked under any of the following circumstances— (1) On or within 5 feet of the traveled portion of a public street or highway;

points.text: It must not be parked on private property (including the premises of a fueling or eating facility) without the knowledge and consent of the person in charge of the property who is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials it contains.
points.quote: On private property (including premises of fueling or eating facility) without the knowledge and consent of the person who is in charge of the property and who is aware of the nature of the hazardous materials the vehicle contains

points.text: It must not be parked within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, dwelling, or place where people work, congregate or assemble, except for brief periods when the necessities of operation require it and make it impracticable to park anywhere else.
points.quote: Within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, dwelling, or place where people work, congregate, or assemble, except for brief periods when the necessities of operation require the vehicle to be parked and make it impracticable to park the vehicle in any other place.

points.text: A vehicle containing hazardous materials other than Division 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 materials must not be parked on or within five feet of the traveled portion of a public street or highway, except for brief periods when the necessities of operation require it and make it impracticable to park anywhere else.
points.quote: A motor vehicle which contains hazardous materials other than Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials must not be parked on or within five feet of the traveled portion of public street or highway except for brief periods when the necessities of operation require the vehicle to be parked and make it impracticable to park the vehicle in any other place.

points.text: A vehicle containing hazardous materials must not be operated near an open fire unless the driver has first taken precautions to ascertain that it can safely pass the fire without stopping, and must not be parked within 300 feet of an open fire.
points.quote: A motor vehicle containing hazardous materials must not be operated near an open fire unless its driver has first taken precautions to ascertain that the vehicle can safely pass the fire without stopping. (b) A motor vehicle containing hazardous materials must not be parked within 300 feet of an open fire.

points.quote: No person may smoke or carry a lighted cigarette, cigar, or pipe on or within 25 feet of— (a) A motor vehicle which contains Class 1 materials, Class 5 materials, or flammable materials classified as Division 2.1, Class 3, Divisions 4.1 and 4.2

points.quote: An empty tank motor vehicle which has been used to transport Class 3, flammable materials, or Division 2.1 flammable gases, which when so used, was required to be marked or placarded in accordance with the rules in § 177.823 of this title.

points.text: When a vehicle containing hazardous materials is being fueled, its engine must not be operating and a person must be in control of the fueling process at the point where the fuel tank is filled.
points.quote: When a motor vehicle which contains hazardous materials is being fueled— (a) Its engine must not be operating; and (b) A person must be in control of the fueling process at the point where the fuel tank is filled.

points.text: The driver must examine each tire on the vehicle at the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked.
points.quote: A driver must examine each tire on a motor vehicle at the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked.

points.text: If a tire is found to be flat, leaking or improperly inflated, at an examination or otherwise, the driver must cause it to be repaired, replaced or properly inflated before the vehicle is driven; however, the vehicle may be driven to the nearest safe place to perform the repair, replacement or inflation.
points.quote: If, as the result of an examination pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section, or otherwise, a tire if found to be flat, leaking, or improperly inflated, the driver must cause the tire to be repaired, replaced, or properly inflated before the vehicle is driven. source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 397.17, Tires (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.quote: A motor carrier that transports Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 (explosive) materials must furnish the driver of each motor vehicle in which the explosives are transported with the following documents: (1) A copy of the rules in this part;

points.text: A motor carrier carrying hazardous materials required to be placarded or marked under 177.823 and not subject to NRHM routing designations must use routes that do not go through or near heavily populated areas, places where crowds are assembled, tunnels, narrow streets or alleys, except where the motor carrier determines that one of the listed exceptions applies.

points.quote: (1) There is no practicable alternative; (2) A reasonable deviation is necessary to reach terminals, points of loading and unloading, facilities for food, fuel, repairs, rest, or a safe haven; or (3) A reasonable deviation is required by emergency conditions, such as a detour that has been established by a highway authority, or a situation exists where a law enforcement official requires the driver to take an alternative route.

points.text: Safety training covers emergency response information, measures to protect the employee from the hazards of materials they may be exposed to (including the employer's specific measures), and methods and procedures for avoiding accidents.
points.quote: (3) Safety training. Each hazmat employee shall receive safety training concerning— (i) Emergency response information required by subpart G of part 172; (ii) Measures to protect the employee from the hazards associated with hazardous materials to which they may be exposed in the work place, including specific measures the hazmat employer has implemented to protect employees from exposure; and (iii) Methods and procedures for avoiding accidents, such as the proper procedures for handling packages containing hazardous materials.

points.quote: Each hazmat employer must create and retain a record of current training of each hazmat employee, inclusive of the preceding three years, in accordance with this section for as long as that employee is employed by that employer as a hazmat employee and for 90 days thereafter.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.704, Training requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The record must include, among other items, the most recent training completion date, a description, copy or location of the training materials, the name and address of the person providing the training, and certification that the employee has been trained and tested.
points.quote: (2) The most recent training completion date of the hazmat employee's training; (3) A description, copy, or the location of the training materials used to meet the requirements in paragraph (a) of this section; (4) The name and address of the person providing the training; and (5) Certification that the hazmat employee has been trained and tested, as required by this subpart.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 172.704, Training requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)
